clue.text: Hand father wife's fruit

blocks.note: a paw is an animal's hand, and informally a person's
pa is an informal word for father
w is the standard abbreviation for wife in family trees

explanation.surface: Someone passes Dad the bowl of fruit belonging to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as an instruction to hand something over, but 'Hand' is a noun here. The trailing 's is only glue between wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The pawpaw, or papaya, is a tropical tree bearing a large sweet orange-fleshed melon-like crop.

clue.text: Start off national agreements with decrees

indicators.note: the start of the word for agreements comes off, so its opening letter is removed

blocks.note: pacts are agreements, typically between nations

explanation.surface: A government begins a new era by scrapping treaties and ruling by decree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' is an instruction, not a verb meaning begin: PACTS loses its first letter, P.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of parliament are laws, formal orders issued by an authority, just as decrees are.

clue.text: I say, civil engineer is articulate!

blocks.note: 'I', say: the word I is an example of a pronoun
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: An exclamation of admiration at how eloquent a civil engineer turns out to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I say' looks like an old-fashioned exclamation; read it as 'I, for example', a word that is a pronoun. 'Articulate' also pretends to be an adjective, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To articulate words is to speak them clearly, sounding out each syllable distinctly.

clue.text: Strange character differently wired to ordinary

indicators.note: arranging the letters of wired differently makes a new word

blocks.note: anagram fodder, five letters
o is a standard abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: An eccentric person whose brain works differently from the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Differently wired' is an idiom for an unusual mind, which is why the anagram hides so well. O level was the old British school exam at ordinary level.
explanation.definitionFit: A weirdo is slang for an odd, eccentric person who behaves oddly or unconventionally.

clue.text: Fine male member captivating a large European

indicators.note: to captivate is to take captive, so the member holds the next pieces inside it

blocks.note: the male member, anatomically
the letter A as it stands
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A handsome club member charms a big fellow from the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' looks like an adjective praising the member, but it is the verb. A and L go inside PENIS, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To fine someone is to punish them with a monetary charge, one form of imposing a penalty.

clue.text: Health professional advocating exercises for hysteria post hip fracture?

indicators.note: a fracture breaks something apart, so the letters of the preceding words are broken up and reset

blocks.note: anagram fodder, fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A clinician prescribes exercises to calm a patient panicking after breaking a hip.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the surface is a joke: the physio really would treat someone after a hip fracture, but here 'fracture' breaks the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiotherapists treat injury by movement and exercise programmes, so they are clinicians who recommend workouts.

clue.text: Mounted soldier's chief replaced by new Scandinavian invader

indicators.note: the chief, or first, letter of the soldier is swapped out for the next item

blocks.note: a soldier on horseback, a cavalryman
n is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A cavalry officer's commander is swapped out for a newly arrived Viking raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chief' looks like the soldier's commanding officer, but it means his first letter: the H of HORSEMAN becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the Vikings, the medieval raiders from Norway and its neighbours who attacked Britain.

clue.text: Had an inclination for asparagus tip during period of fasting

indicators.note: the tip of the vegetable is its first letter only
during places one thing within a period of time, so the letter sits inside the fast

blocks.note: the first letter of asparagus
Lent is the forty days of Christian fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: Someone who craved asparagus while giving things up for Lent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Had an inclination' reads as a craving, but it is literal: tilted to one side. A goes into LENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Leant is the past tense of lean, meaning tilted or sloped, a physical slant.

clue.text: One ruining the enjoyment of others overindulges on drink

definitions.text: One ruining the enjoyment of others

blocks.note: to spoil a child is to overindulge it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: A killjoy who drinks too much and ruins the party for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The drinking in the surface makes 'drink' look like part of the story, but it is simply the fortified wine. In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoilsport is a killjoy, someone who stops other people having fun.

clue.text: Art nouveau associated with old commercial centre is an abomination

indicators.note: nouveau is French for new, so the preceding word is given a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder, three letters
o is the abbreviation for old
the City is London's financial and business district

explanation.surface: An art critic sneers that Art Nouveau buildings in an old business district are monstrosities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Art nouveau' looks like the design movement, and splits into fodder and instruction. The City is the historic square mile of London that is its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is an appalling, wicked act, as loathsome and shocking as any abomination.

clue.text: Think about a relative

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the letter A as it stands
a son is a family relative

explanation.surface: Someone pondering a member of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and 'about' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason is to use logic, working through a problem mentally to form conclusions.

clue.text: Head off common ailment with view shaped by outdated example of folk wisdom

indicators.note: cutting the head off the ailment means dropping its first letter
a view that is shaped is formed anew, so its letters are remade

blocks.note: the common cold
anagram fodder, four letters
stale means no longer fresh, outdated

explanation.surface: Warding off a cold with an old-fashioned remedy, the kind grandma swore by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like 'prevent', which suits the cold, but it removes the C from COLD. The enumeration is 3,5,4 with an apostrophe after WIVES.
explanation.definitionFit: An old wives' tale is a traditional superstition or piece of popular lore, often untrue.

clue.text: Chap to study fragments of tile with instrument for measuring angles

indicators.note: breaking the tile into fragments scatters its letters into a new order

blocks.note: Theo is a man's name, and 'chap' can stand for any man's name
to do a subject is to study it, as in 'she's doing history'
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: A man sets out to examine broken tiles using a surveying tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chap' can clue any man's name; here it is THEO. DO for study is the student sense: 'I'm doing maths'.
explanation.definitionFit: A theodolite is the tripod-mounted surveyor's telescope that measures horizontal and vertical angles.

clue.text: Body part trapped in machine

indicators.note: something trapped in a word sits inside its letters, waiting to be found

blocks.note: the middle letters of maCHINe

explanation.surface: A factory accident: someone's limb caught in the machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an industrial injury report, which is why the tiny hidden word in 'machine' goes unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: The chin is the lower front of the face, below the mouth, part of the human anatomy.

clue.text: Time passed with group, including priest in part of church

indicators.note: a group including a member holds that member within it

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for time
time ran, meaning it passed
a set is a group
p is a dictionary abbreviation for priest

explanation.surface: Time went by for a congregation whose priest was standing in a side aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passed' is RAN in the sense that time ran on. P for priest is a dictionary abbreviation rather than an everyday one.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church building, crossing the nave at right angles.

clue.text: Reputations built up on signs of approval heard for study of meaning

indicators.note: in a down clue, building upward means reading the word from bottom to top
heard means we want what the approval marks sound like, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: a good name is a good reputation
ticks are marks of approval; tics are twitches that sound the same

explanation.surface: Careers made on marks of approval, as in a student chasing grades in linguistics.
explanation.walkthrough: A tick is the British mark for a correct answer, which Americans call a check mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Semantics is the branch of linguistics concerned with what words and sentences signify.

clue.text: More cuts baffled one paying for services

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so the letters of the preceding words are mixed up

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: A bank client is bewildered by yet another round of service reductions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about austerity; 'baffled' looks like a reaction but tells you to rearrange the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is a client or purchaser who buys goods or pays a business for work.

clue.text: Simplest unit in compound found by spy with cryptic clue

indicators.note: a cryptic clue is puzzling and disguised, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
anagram fodder, four letters

explanation.surface: A secret agent tracks down the basic element of a secret chemical formula using a coded tip-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compound' suggests a walled camp for a spy story, but it is the chemical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A molecule is the smallest particle of a chemical substance that keeps its properties, bonded atoms together.

clue.text: Global food giant spoils planet

blocks.note: a multinational confectionery and pet-food corporation, maker of a famous chocolate bar
to mar is to spoil
the fourth planet from the sun

explanation.surface: A multinational food corporation is accused of wrecking the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: This is really three definitions in a row: the company, the verb 'spoils', and the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars is at once a confectionery corporation, a verb for damaging, and the red fourth world from the sun.

clue.text: Poems associated with South American port

blocks.note: odes are lyric poems
SA is an abbreviation for South America

explanation.surface: Verses connected to a harbour city in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American port' reads as one phrase, sending you to Brazil or Chile; the definition is only 'port', and it is on the Black Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Ukrainian seaport city on the Black Sea coast.

clue.text: Company outlet released designer's first range in part of central London

indicators.note: the designer's first is the opening letter of that word
the letters that follow are let loose and fall into a new order

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a vent is an outlet for air or steam
the opening letter of designer
anagram fodder with the designer's initial

explanation.surface: A fashion firm's shop launches a designer's first collection in a trendy London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a fashion launch: 'outlet', 'released' and 'range' all feel like retail words. Covent Garden is a shopping and theatre district in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden is a West End district of the capital, known for its market, opera house and shops.

clue.text: Lover at Olympus embracing Greek muse

indicators.note: the opening words hold the answer within their letters, as arms hold someone

blocks.note: spans the end of loVER, all of AT and the O of Olympus

explanation.surface: A god's lover on Mount Olympus hugs one of the nine Muses.
explanation.walkthrough: The mythological surface makes a hidden word unlikely, but the muse spans three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato was one of the nine Muses of Greek mythology, the patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Prohibit importing English vegetable

indicators.note: to import is to bring something in, so the ban takes the next piece inside

blocks.note: to ban is to prohibit
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A trade embargo on English produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Importing' sounds like trade policy, which fits the surface, but it puts E inside BAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Beans are edible seeds or pods from leguminous plants, eaten as greens or pulses.

clue.text: Win over maids prepared to capture king

indicators.note: prepared means made ready, a remaking of the servants' letters
capturing someone means holding them, so the maids hold the monarch inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, five letters
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Household servants plot to seize the monarch and so charm their way into favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Win over' is a phrasal verb meaning charm; it is not a chess or battle win.
explanation.definitionFit: To disarm someone figuratively is to charm them, dispelling their hostility or suspicion.

clue.text: Sin (pride) beaten with divine intervention

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked out of shape, so the letters take a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, eight letters

explanation.surface: The deadly sin of pride is defeated when God steps in.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket makes the surface read as a note on which sin is meant; typographically it is just two words of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspired originally meant breathed into by God, so a thing inspired came through heavenly influence.

clue.text: Appear to backtrack during expression of annoyance with Obama?

indicators.note: going back over the same path means reading the verb from right to left
during puts one thing within another, so the turned verb goes inside the exclamation

blocks.note: to come on stage is to appear
drat is a mild curse

explanation.surface: A politician seems to reverse a position while voicing frustration at the president.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Obama is an example: he is one member of the party, not a synonym for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama was the US president elected for the Democratic Party, one of its best-known figures.

clue.text: Sailor told to go away

blocks.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
someone told to go has been sent

explanation.surface: A seaman is ordered off the ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Told to go away' reads as one dismissal; the definition is just the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be away is to be not present, missing from where one would normally be.
